text: The handle's read verbs are get, connect with disconnect, changes and past; the older verbs here and asOf are gone, and tap is no longer a sink.
evidence: READS 7; CONNECT 8.4; LAYERS 3.7 D2

text: Rows that tie in an ordered view are ordered by row key, compared in UTF-16 code units.
evidence: E-23; E-57 A3, B1, XB-2 (0 unequal; each planted bug failed 159 to 1,000 of 1,000 seeds)

text: Each direction has one total order over every value: descending (za) is numbers from high to low, then every other value in the ascending (az) order.
A sum is exact over every finite number whatever the order of arrival; minus zero is kept, and NaN and the two infinities are counted apart from the sum.
evidence: E-23 (float sums differed from the exact sum in 97 to 99 % of checks); E-57 XB-4

text: distinct keeps, for each value, the row with the smallest key.
A bucket is dropped when its last row leaves.
exportContract() states for each call whether it is plain data, how its parts merge (by rows, by adding, by the best or by the top k) and what class of cost it has.
evidence: TRANSFORMS 9.1 C6; MERGE 2, 5.5 pick 6 (fero's merger reads the merge class); E-57 XA-9 checked the cap on a guessed cost model, not the export

text: limit and reverse over rows with no order are marked as depending on arrival; limit over a sorted parent reads the parent's order.
evidence: E-57 XB-13 (today's limit fails 1,000 of 1,000 seeds over a sorted parent)

text: top(n) over object rows throws.
evidence: TRANSFORMS 9.1 C8; the ground probe shows today's fault (it acts as limit(n))

text: sum, avg, min, max, the quantiles, buckets with a step and the range filters all read a field through one numeric projection: a value that is not a number, by type, takes no part.
evidence: E-57 XB-3 and the max probe (today a string passes a range filter, and min and max over a mixed column depend on arrival)

text: by, eq, in and distinct compare values by type with SameValueZero, and a bucket's key keeps its type.
eq and in are row filters written as plain data, over scalar values only.
by(field, { step }) keeps one aggregate per bucket, and its answer is a Map whose keys keep their type; step takes finite numbers only.
group, distinct, some and every take a field name, and that form is plain data.
az and za take a count and an after cursor of value then key, and every page reader of one field and direction reads one shared ordered index.
evidence: E-57 B2, XA-7 (a page read 10 to 16 µs on one shared index)

text: lookup(otherSource, field) joins each left row to the other source's row of that key, and keeps a reverse index so a change on the other side reaches every left row that names it.
evidence: E-57 B4, XB-11 (537,670 checks, 0 unequal; the reverse index not moved on a field change fails 1,000 of 1,000 seeds)

text: An ordered mirror source applies wire records that carry a place or a move, and hands its order to the operators after it.
A key iterator walks a source's keys in steps that can stop and go on later, without copying the store.
evidence: E-57 XA-1 (listing keys copies the store today)

text: eq, in, by and lookup are reserved operator names: a row or field with one of those names is read only through get(key), never as a property.
evidence: TRANSFORMS 9.1 (data's own rule that a new operator name is claimed only in a major, checked in data contract/index.ts); LAYERS 3.7 N1, N2, N5

text: A view can run over the rows of one group alone, inside the one store of its resource.
evidence: MERGE 6 item 4; LAYERS 3.7, 4.6 (owed)

text: An exact sum hands out its whole state, and two states can be added or one taken away from another with no loss.
evidence: MERGE 5.5 pick 6, 6 (30 to 50 lines, a guess); E-57 XB-4 for the exact sum itself

text: A partial's max and distinct keep an index per bucket, so a row that leaves is replaced without a pass over the bucket.
evidence: LAYERS 4.6 (owed); V5-22 owed list

text: A change reaches only the path subscriptions on the keys it touches, found through an index by key, so the cost of a write does not grow with the number of path readers.
evidence: E-55 claim 8 (10,000 path lenses cost 1.09 to 1.52 times no lens on the prototype, against about 120 times today); LENS 4.5

text: Every sink is called once per commit with the value and one commit object, both by reference; the commit object carries the diff, and for an ordered view the order.
evidence: E-55 claim 10 (63 to 122 ns a commit); E-57 XA-5; LENS 4.5

text: A commit object's recs() and text() are made once and shared by every sink of that commit.
evidence: LAYERS 3.7 D4

text: A row is frozen the first time it is handed out, to a reader or to a sink, and not before.
evidence: LENS 2.7, 4.5; REQUIREMENTS DATA-07

text: Each diff entry carries the version of its row, read from the version column.
evidence: READS 2.1; LAYERS 3.7 N7; COMPACT 5 fix 3

text: A source writes its rows out as key, version and bytes under a format id, and loads them back through the store; it never dumps the engine's own objects.
evidence: COMPACT 5 fix 2; LAYERS 3.7

text: A source keeps its key index in many small tables chosen by the key's hash, so no single table grows in one long step and a source can pass 16,777,216 rows.
evidence: E-66 (64 tables: every rebuild under 20 ms, past 16,777,216 keys; one table stalls 631 to 688 ms at 8.4e6 keys); COMPACT 5 fix 6

text: The store keeps each row's version in a column of its own, by the row's place in the store, read by key; the version is never a field of the row handed out and never a separate map.
evidence: E-62 item 4 (8 to 16 B a row; a separate map costs +8 to +397 ns a write); COMPACT 5 fix 3

text: A source can list, snapshot and drop the rows of one slot without walking every row of the store.
evidence: GROUPS G7 (a move must take one slot's rows out of a store; +1 rule in data); BUILD 3.5 slice 3

text: Two reads of a row that has not changed give the same object.
evidence: data 4's code (true today); COMPACT 5 fix 5; LAYERS 3.2

text: A source can hold rows in two levels, partition then row, and an operator can run inside one partition.
evidence: E-55 claim 19 (a one-row partition costs about 0.9 KB more and 1.3 to 1.5 times the fold); LENS 4.5

text: A view over a whole two-level source keys, breaks ties and pages by the pair of partition and row.
A dropped source frees its rows and its indexes.
evidence: E-65 X1 probe-drop shows the need (18 to 23 MB per 1e5 rows stay after a drop today); the fix is not built

text: A store reports how many bytes it keeps a row, so a hold can be judged against the memory limit before it opens.
evidence: COMPACT 5 fix 1 and 6 (API.md 9: the open asks data's store for its bytes a row)

text: A view belongs to the handle or the handler call it was made in, and ends when that ends; no sink of it is called after.
evidence: E-55 claim 26 (0 calls after the end in 59,958 view sinks); E-56 probe 4; E-57 A6

text: An operator chain is plain data that can be sent and built again elsewhere, and an ordered view's order travels beside its rows.
evidence: E-55 claim 17 (a plain keyed copy of an ordered view was wrong in 239 of 1,000 runs); E-57 A7

text: group sends one change per row into its bucket, never the whole bucket again.
evidence: E-05; E-57 B2 (the deltas checked exact; group(fn) costs 78 to 94 ms a change at 1e6 rows today)

text: An ordered view (az, za, top) keeps its rows in a chunked index that costs O(log N) for a single write and for a batch, and a page reader reads it with no window.
evidence: E-57 XB-1 (9.5 to 15.1 µs a write at 1e6 rows, from 1,305 to 1,385; above a guessed bar of 3); E-65

text: Every view builds in slices that can stop and go on later, whatever its operators.
evidence: E-57 XA-1 (a build over 1e6 rows blocks 0.49 to 1.9 s in one piece today; sliced, 0.21 to 0.24 s on the prototype's own nodes, a missed bar; the ordered index could not be sliced from outside)

text: A view is not equal to its query until its build ends, and it says when it is ready.
evidence: TRANSFORMS 9.1 D9 (a SCHEDULE clause, and perhaps a ready state)

text: An operator keeps keys and the values it projects, never whole rows, and a full pass goes through each or the key iterator, never a new snapshot() call on a hot path.
evidence: E-66 (4 node classes always keep rows, 3 more when the projection is the row); COMPACT 5 fix 4

text: median, quantile and percentile keep their values in sorted chunks, so a change does not move the whole column.
evidence: E-65 shows the need (today a median costs 0.15 to 0.19 ms a write at 1e6 rows); EVERYROW 0 item 7 (a chunked index should fix it, reasoned); not built or timed in data
